newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia plans SKK 14 bln in 1997 highway building.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia plans SKK 14 bln in 1997 highway building.

text.p: Slovakia plans to spend 14 billion crowns in 1997 on motorway construction, with more than half financed by foreign and domestic credit, the state agency managing financing of the projects said on Thursday.

The director of the state fund for road construction, Jozef Polcic, told Reuters the fund had already signed loan deals with the largest Slovak credit bank VUB a.s. and the state-run savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna a.s.
"Both credits were worth one billion crowns, and they carry an interest rate of BRIBOR (Bratislava Interbank Offer Rate) plus two percent," Polcic told Reuters.
The BRIBOR on Thursday ranged from 15.47 percent to 16.18 percent.
The loans cover investment in the first quarter of this year, and delayed repayment will run from 1999 to 2006.
Investment in the second quarter should be covered in part by funds from the issue of state bonds, which are planned to total roughly five billion crowns, Polcic said.
The plan is also to draw bank credits totalling 7.2 billion crowns for motorway construction in the second half of 1997.
"We expect to sign a 40 million ECU loan, about 1.2 billion crowns, with the European Investment Bank (EIB), which should be drawn in the second half of the year," Polcic said.
Conditions of the credit facilities will be agreed shortly before signing the loans, according to the market situation, Polcic said.
He said that so far the agency has had no problem in finding credit sources for financing the project.
The agency had been offered a three billion crown credit from the largest Czech saving bank Ceska Sporitelna, and an unspecified tranche from the consortium of domestic banks.
All banks, except Slovenska Sporitelna, demand state guarantess, Polcic said.
He added that Japan's Exim bank had shown interest in taking part in the Slovak motorway construction programme.
The remaining 1.8 billion crowns for the 1997 investment plans will be covered from the fund's own resources.

Slovakia plans to build 491 km of motorway by the year 2005, bringing the total length of its motorway system to 689 km. The total cost of construction is estimated at 134 billion Slovak crowns ($4.49 billion).
